name: Hamilton / Richmond Hill (formerly Pearson Airport Express)
description: An airport express that began between Square One, Pearson and Richmond Hill Centre, became a two-terminal Pearson–Richmond Hill shuttle, and later expanded west to Hamilton. Its history includes short express branches and, in 2026, Humber and Unionville service.

timeline.event: Route 40 begins with half-hourly Square One–Pearson service; alternate trips continue to Richmond Hill Centre, giving that segment hourly service.
The original timetable documents an hourly Square One–Pearson–Richmond Hill pattern seven days a week.
The route has been shortened to Pearson Terminal 1–Richmond Hill Centre; Square One is absent from the effective January 1 timetable.
Route 40 expands to Hamilton and takes over the former 47J Hamilton–Square One express service; GO’s ridership report gives this exact date.
Highway 407 Bus Terminal opens. The January 2019 route 40 timetable confirms the new terminal, Dixie and Renforth as main-route stops.
40A runs Hamilton–Square One express, bypassing Trafalgar/407; 40B provides a Richmond Hill Centre–Pearson short express that bypasses Highway 407 terminal.

The timetable includes 40H and 40M via Humber Polytechnic North Campus, with 40M continuing to Unionville. Dundas/407 is also on the main route by this snapshot. This change accompanies the withdrawal of routes 54 and 66.

name: Hamilton / Pickering; earlier Orangeville route number
description: The number has two unrelated eras. Before April 28, 2008, 41 identified Orangeville service, which became route 37. The new Hamilton–Pickering route 41 was created in 2021 by joining the former Highway 407 West and East services.

timeline.event: The contemporary April 2008 service notice identifies the then-existing Orangeville service as route 41.

Orangeville route 41 is renumbered 37. This earlier route is geographically and historically separate from the Hamilton–Pickering route introduced in 2021. See route 37 for the continuing Orangeville family.
New route 41 combines most weekday trips on routes 47 and 51. Metrolinx announces 38 weekday trips and a through ride without transferring at Highway 407 Bus Terminal.

The original main-route pattern runs via McMaster, the western park-and-rides, Square One, Bramalea, Richmond Hill Centre, Consumers Road, Scarborough Centre and the two Scarborough campuses. It does not serve Unionville.
41A appears as a school-oriented express pattern; an explicitly timed trip runs Square One–Bramalea–Highway 407–Consumers Road–Centennial–UTSC, bypassing Richmond Hill Centre and Scarborough Centre.

name: Bolton (renumbered 38 in 2008)
description: The earlier Bolton GO bus number, linked to York Mills through Yorkdale, Etobicoke North, Woodbridge, Kleinburg and Nobleton. The contemporary 2008 notice explicitly establishes the 42-to-38 renumbering; this is stronger evidence than the older Table 42 label alone.

timeline.event: Original Table 42 documents the weekday York Mills–Yorkdale–Etobicoke North–Bolton service through Woodbridge, Kleinburg and Nobleton. Union Station times are connecting trains, not a through bus to Bolton.

The original PDF shows two southbound morning and two northbound afternoon weekday bus trips, with rail connections at Etobicoke North. The archive filename says February 2008, but the timetable itself is dated September 4, 2004.
GO renumbers Bolton route 42 as route 38. The continuing corridor belongs to the route 38 history.

name: Mount Pleasant / McMaster University; earlier Wonderland route number

timeline.event: Original Wonderland Table 43 shows a seasonal service between Canada’s Wonderland, Yorkdale Subway and York Mills Subway, with separate seasonal fares. The surviving page displays July 1, 2003 service.
The Wonderland service resumes under number 60, replacing number 43, according to the contemporary April 22 service notice.

A new, unrelated route 43 appears in the effective September 5 timetable: Mount Pleasant GO to McMaster via Mississauga Road, Meadowvale, Trafalgar/407 and Dundas/407. It operates weekdays excluding holidays.

Public routes 45 and 45A are printed explicitly: Streetsville–Square One–Keele–York and a Square One short working. Both bypass Bramalea.
Erin Mills Transitway Station opens to GO service; it is included on route 45 in the September 2018 original.
Main 45 serves Erin Mills and continues to York via Keele. Unlike the stopping 46/47/48 patterns, 45 and 45A bypass the newly opened Highway 407 Bus Terminal.
GO leaves York University campus; later 2019 route 45 timetables terminate at Highway 407 Bus Terminal.
45B is a Streetsville–Erin Mills–Square One–Highway 407–Richmond Hill Centre–Unionville through branch, bypassing Bramalea.
Route 45 is discontinued in the spring service revision.

name: Hamilton / Highway 407 (formerly York University and Yorkdale)
description: The Hamilton and McMaster arm of the 407 network has had numerous express, short and weekend branches. Suffixes have been reused: the older 47D was a Bramalea–York short route, while the 2023 47D is a McMaster express; the older 47G extended to Yorkdale.

timeline.event: The Highway 407 network expands to Hamilton and McMaster University, the predecessor of numbered route 47.
The original Hamilton–McMaster–407 park-and-rides–Square One–Bramalea–York pattern is documented.
The original has branches 47A/B/C/D/E/F/G/H. Weekend 47G runs beyond York University to Yorkdale; 47D is a short Bramalea–Keele–York service.
47J provides Hamilton–Trafalgar/407–Square One service, bypassing McMaster and the western 407 park-and-rides.
47J is absorbed into the extended route 40.
The main route serves Erin Mills and Highway 407 terminal before Keele and York. Express McMaster variants remain.
The York University terminus is replaced by Highway 407 Bus Terminal.
Most weekday 47 trips combine with 51 into new through route 41; route 47 remains as a separate family.
Seasonal 47W extends via Canada’s Wonderland to Major Mackenzie/Hwy. 400 Park & Ride.
The timetable uses 47D for McMaster–Square One–Bramalea–Highway 407 express service and 47G for a McMaster–Erin Mills stopping short route. These differ from the 2011 suffix meanings.
Weekday route 47 service is increased to roughly half-hourly in the spring revision.
Seasonal Wonderland service uses the new Major Mackenzie West Terminal in 2023.

description: A Meadowvale–Bramalea–York corridor expanded west to the University of Guelph through Aberfoyle. It retained direct student expresses and short Meadowvale workings alongside the stopping route.

timeline.event: Table 46 shows Meadowvale–Bramalea–York and a direct Meadowvale–York predecessor express.
Government releases document the Guelph–Aberfoyle–Meadowvale expansion. The August announcement gave September 3, while the November retrospective says service began September 4.
Main 48 runs Guelph–Aberfoyle–Meadowvale–Hurontario/407–Bramalea–Keele–York. 48A bypasses Hurontario and Bramalea, while 48B is the stopping Meadowvale short route.
Main 48 and 48B call at Highway 407 terminal before York, while 48A bypasses it. 48F is a limited Guelph–Bramalea–Highway 407–Keele–York express.
GO leaves York campus and the route’s eastern end becomes Highway 407 Bus Terminal.

timeline.event: The original 407 corridor is extended to Scarborough Town Centre, a predecessor of route 51.
The eastern service is extended to Pickering via Centennial College and UTSC.
The public route column documents 51, Scarborough Centre express 51A and Pickering express 51B. Main 51 uses Langstaff’s south lot and bypasses Unionville.
Richmond Hill Centre replaces Langstaff in the timetable. Keele/Great Gulf is now listed, and 51C directly connects the Scarborough campuses with Keele and York.
51D is a Richmond Hill Centre–Centennial–UTSC short express. Main 51 serves Kingston/Fairport rather than the earlier Highway 2/Liverpool timing point.

Routes end at Highway 407 Bus Terminal instead of York. The 51B express calls at Brock/407 between Pickering and the terminal; 51C serves the Scarborough campuses, and 51D still starts at Richmond Hill Centre.
Most weekday 51 trips combine with route 47 to create route 41.

name: Oshawa / Highway 407 (formerly Oshawa / York University)
description: The Oshawa arm of Highway 407 East, with multiple campus expresses, a move from Langstaff to Richmond Hill Centre, terminal changes in Vaughan and Oshawa, and later use of Highway 407 across Durham. Twenty documentary corridor reconstructions cover the predecessor service and changing branches.

timeline.event: Oshawa–York service begins, with nine weekday trips each way. The contemporary newspaper report and York University article establish the original corridor before public route numbering.
Numbered 52 runs York–Langstaff–Unionville–Brock/407–Greenwood–Brooklin–Durham College/UOIT–Oshawa terminal. 52A is a Unionville–campus short route via the Durham roadside stops.

The original replaces Langstaff with Richmond Hill Centre and explicitly serves Keele at Great Gulf Dr. westbound / Snidercroft eastbound. Example: 06:05 Oshawa, 07:07 Richmond Hill Centre, 07:18 Keele, 07:25 York.
The Durham route uses the Lake Ridge/Highway 7 timing point instead of Greenwood. The timetable includes an express Unionville–campus 52A and a campus–Richmond Hill–Keele–York 52B.
Highway 407 Bus Terminal opens.
GO leaves York campus. Route 52 terminates at Highway 407; the timetable includes Unionville express 52D and campus express 52B.
The original timetable replaces the former Oshawa Bus Terminal terminus with downtown street stops and an extension to Oshawa GO.
Most weekday 52 trips join route 46 as new route 56; 52 remains a separate route, especially for weekend and special patterns.
The 52A suffix now marks the stopping route with Baldwin/407 added; this differs from its earlier campus-express meaning.
Seasonal 52X runs to Canada’s Wonderland and Major Mackenzie/Hwy. 400 Park & Ride.
Cornell Bus Terminal is added to routes 52 and 56.
52 and 56 move from the Highway 7/Winchester corridor to Highway 407 between the Brock and Simcoe areas, removing the Lake Ridge and Winchester/Anderson stops from the main route.
Seasonal 52X uses Major Mackenzie West Terminal for Wonderland access.
A campus express version skips Brock, Baldwin, downtown Oshawa and Oshawa GO, while serving Cornell, Unionville, Richmond Hill and Highway 407.
The researched 52A express pattern serves Highway 407, Richmond Hill, Unionville, Cornell, the campus, downtown Oshawa and Oshawa GO while bypassing Brock and Baldwin.

name: Mount Joy / York University; later Mount Joy / Highway 407
description: The Markham arm of the Highway 407 network connected Mount Joy, Markham, Centennial and Unionville with Langstaff or Richmond Hill Centre and York University. Expresses served different portions of the Markham corridor. It later terminated at Highway 407 and ended in January 2026.

timeline.event: The original Highway 407 launch reaches Unionville through York University, a predecessor corridor of 54.
The timetable explicitly identifies 54 Mount Joy–Markham–Centennial–Unionville–Langstaff–York; 54A starts at Unionville and 54B at Centennial, both bypassing Langstaff.
Richmond Hill Centre replaces Langstaff and the Keele stop is added. 54C connects Mount Joy and Markham directly with Keele and York, bypassing Centennial, Unionville and Richmond Hill Centre.
GO’s York University service ends. The main 54 and its express variants terminate at Highway 407 Bus Terminal.
Route 54 is discontinued as part of the January service changes, with replacement services described in Metrolinx’s announcement and the revised route 40 timetable.

name: Oshawa / Oakville
description: A long through route created in 2021 by joining the Oakville and Oshawa arms of the Highway 407 network. It inherited both the western college/park-and-ride stops and the eastern campus/downtown corridor.

timeline.event: Metrolinx creates route 56 by combining most weekday trips on routes 46 and 52, with 38 weekday through trips announced.

The original labels the principal route 56A and includes the Baldwin/407 detour together with Lake Ridge and Winchester/Anderson. It links Oakville GO and Oshawa GO through Sheridan, Square One, Bramalea, Highway 407 and Richmond Hill Centre.
Cornell Bus Terminal is added. The January 2023 original confirms it.
The Durham part moves onto Highway 407, replacing the Lake Ridge/Winchester street section while retaining Brock/407, Baldwin/407, Ontario Tech/Durham College and Oshawa stops.
